commentary_title: VLCC utilisation strengthens despite weak tonne-mile dmeand
commentary_summary: VLCC utilisation improved to 92.3% in week 40, up 1.6 percentage points MoM and YoY, suggesting stronger fleet employment despite subdued demand indicators. However, the tonne-mile index remained weak at 87.5, down 2.2% YoY, suggesting that reduced voyage distances and softer long-haul crude movements continue to weigh on underlying transport demand. | Market activity showed signs of regional divergence, with vessel capacity at anchor declining by 4.1% MoM in the west and 0.5% in the east. Higher ballast speeds in the east point to active fleet repositioning and improving vessel availability, while the recovery in the tonne-mile index from recent lows indicates some improvement in cargo flows heading into the fourth quarter. | Easing congestion and faster vessel turnaround continued to lift effective fleet supply. Lower anchorage levels, combined with elevated ballast and laden sailing speeds, increased tonnage availability across key trading regions, offsetting support from stronger utilisation and limiting the upside for VLCC freight rates despite firmer bunker prices.
